section_summary: This section centers on Hiram Bingham Jr.’s report “Criminal Statistics as Kept in Japan,” transmitted by the American Consulate General in January 1930. The report explains Japan’s centralized collection of police, prison, and court statistics and reproduces extensive national and Hyogo Prefecture tables, prison reporting forms, and historical crime data. The closing documents record the report’s distribution to the National Commission on Law Observance and Enforcement and the Department of Justice, followed by the State Department’s acknowledgment and “EXCELLENT” rating.

subfiles.title: Criminal Statistics as Kept in Japan
subfiles.from: Hiram Bingham Jr., American Vice Consul
subfiles.to: U.S. Department of State and National Commission on Law Observance and Enforcement
subfiles.about: Describes the Japanese system for collecting police, prison, and court statistics and supplies translated examples of official tables and reporting forms.
subfiles.summary: The report explains how Japan’s centralized administration, family-register system, prefectural reporting, and national ministries produced detailed criminal statistics. It reproduces extensive 1928 Hyogo police data on offenses, arrests, penalties, suicides, theft, robbery, prosecutions, warrants, and public protection, followed by prison population tables and translated forms for the admission, release, and punishment of prisoners. A final section outlines the 88 tables in the Imperial Department of Justice’s 1927 criminal-case report and presents national figures on proceedings, trial duration, judgments, punishments, criminal actions, murder, and arson. The report concludes by identifying official publications, the Japan Year Books, the Census Register Law, newspaper reports, and interviews in Kobe and Tokyo as its sources.
